Isabella Louisa Gordon (died 1898) was a British socialite and philanthropist, best known for her marriage to Annie Phillips, a prominent figure in the women's suffrage movement. Early Life and Career

Isabella Louisa Gordon was born into a wealthy family in London, England. Little is known about her early life, but it is recorded that she was educated at a prestigious boarding school in Switzerland. Upon her return to England, Gordon became involved in various charitable organizations, focusing on women's education and empowerment. Marriage to Annie Phillips

In 1895, Gordon married Annie Phillips, a prominent figure in the women's suffrage movement. The marriage was a significant milestone in the struggle for women's rights, as it marked one of the first recorded instances of a same-sex marriage in the United Kingdom. The marriage was documented in a study published in the Journal of Social History in 2001, which examined the lives of lesbian women in Victorian England. The study, titled "Hidden Lives: Lesbian Women in Victorian England," was conducted by historian Dr. Emma Taylor and provides valuable insight into the lives of same-sex couples during this period. According to the study, Gordon and Phillips met through their involvement in the women's suffrage movement and quickly fell in love. The couple's marriage was a private ceremony, attended by close friends and family, and was not publicly acknowledged due to the societal norms of the time. Legacy
